artists.biography: Split Enz were a New Zealand band of the 1970s and early 1980s featuring Phil Judd and brothers Tim Finn and Neil Finn. They achieved chart success in New Zealand, Australia, and Canada during the early 1980s’ most notably with the single "I Got You", and built a cult following elsewhere. Their musical style was eclectic and original, incorporating influences from art rock, vaudeville, swing, punk, rock, new wave, and pop.

Split Enz.biography: Split Enz were a New Zealand band of the 1970s and early 1980s featuring Phil Judd and brothers Tim Finn and Neil Finn. They achieved chart success in New Zealand, Australia, and Canada during the early 1980s’ most notably with the single "I Got You", and built a cult following elsewhere. Their musical style was eclectic and original, incorporating influences from art rock, vaudeville, swing, punk, rock, new wave, and pop.

perplexity.description:
True Colours, released in January 1980, is the sixth studio album by New Zealand band Split Enz and marks their first major commercial success. The album showcases a blend of electronic, rock, and pop styles, with a distinctive new wave influence that was prominent in the late 1970s and early 1980s. It features more pronounced contributions from co-lead singer and songwriter Neil Finn, whose involvement helped shape the band's evolving sound during this period.

Musically, True Colours is characterized by its polished production, catchy melodies, and the integration of synthesizers and electronic textures alongside traditional rock instrumentation. This stylistic shift contributed to its broad appeal and commercial breakthrough, especially with standout tracks like "I Got You" becoming hits. Released on Mushroom Records in Australasia and A&M Records internationally, the album solidified Split Enz's place in the pop/rock landscape of the era and is often regarded as a defining work in their discography.
